question: Where can I get a list of LNG terminals and underground gas storage facilities in the United States, with location, operator, capacity and status?

answer.summary: Underground storage: EIA's EIA-191 field data (API, monthly to Aug 2026) gives operator, county, Active/Inactive, working gas and max daily withdrawal; PHMSA's annual UNGS file adds exact coordinates. LNG: PHMSA's annual file lists 191 regulated plants (186 in service) with operator, state/ZIP, status and liquefaction/vaporization/tank capacity; EIA's quarterly file gives export trains operating, under construction or approved. Proposed terminals and storage projects are only in FERC PDF maps and Federal Register notices; exact LNG plant positions are restricted (NPMS).
main_caveats: Different publishers measure LNG capacity differently: PHMSA reports maximum liquefaction rate (Sabine Pass 5100 MMCF/D), EIA nameplate per train (6 x 0.59 Bcf/d baseload, 0.76 peak).
PHMSA field TOTAL_CAPACITY_MMCF is maximum vaporization in MMCF per day, not storage volume; LNG tank storage is TOTAL_CAPACITY_BBLS (barrels).
EIA Maximum Daily Delivery is a withdrawal rate. PHMSA injected and withdrawn values are annual volumes. Facility-level maximum injection rates were not verified.
phmsa.dot.gov, ferc.gov and maritime.dot.gov reject automated clients (403); the PHMSA ZIPs are also attached to data.transportation.gov dataset aemm-7pyq, but that copy lags (2024 data).

Offshore LNG deepwater ports are licensed by MARAD, not FERC; FERC lists cover onshore/near-shore terminals only, and most of the 170+ LNG plants (utility peakshavers, satellites) are not FERC-jurisdictional.
answer.confidence_reason: Core EIA and PHMSA files were downloaded and checked; PHMSA 2025 data came from an archived copy, and the FERC PDF maps and MARAD pages could not be read because they block automated clients.

attributes.note: Storage: exact lat/lon per facility (PHMSA) and county (EIA). LNG: state and ZIP (PHMSA) or state only (EIA); no official LNG coordinates published.
attributes.gap_note: LNG plant positions sit in PHMSA's NPMS: PIMMA is restricted to government officials and operators; the public viewer hides LNG plants below ~1:24,000. GEM coordinates are form-gated.

attributes.note: Operator per storage facility and LNG plant (PHMSA operator ID and name; EIA-191 respondent); EIA liquefaction file names the project sponsor.
Storage: working/base/total gas (Mcf or BCF) and max daily withdrawal (Mcf/d); LNG: liquefaction and vaporization MMCF/D, tanks bbl, nameplate Bcf/d-Mtpa. No injection rate.
attributes.gap_note: The sources checked give working volume and withdrawal rates for underground storage. Facility-level maximum injection rates were not verified.

attributes.note: Storage Active/Inactive (EIA); LNG In Service/Retired/Abandoned (PHMSA); export trains operating/commissioning/under construction/approved (EIA); FERC PDF maps add proposed.
attributes.gap_note: No structured official list of proposed LNG import terminals, proposed peakshavers or planned storage projects; they appear only in FERC PDF maps and FERC notices (Federal Register).

how_to_use.example_result: {"a": 2024, "b": "TX", "id": "03600004TX", "c": 370123, "d": 1, "e": "ENSTOR KATY STORAGE & TRANSPLP", "f": "KATY HUB & STOR", "g": "FULSHEAR (HILLE", "h": "Depleted Field", "i": "Fort Bend", "k": "Active", "m": 23500000, "n": 31300000, "o": 700000, "l": 7800000, "j": "South Central Region"} (one of 414 rows)
steps: Request data/report/RP7/data/{year1}/{year2} (annual, 2005-2024) or data/report/RP8/data/{year1}/{year2} (monthly, 2014-2026) under https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/ngqs/.
The JSON has 'columns' (field letter to header) and 'data' (rows); map letters with 'columns' because RP7 and RP8 use different letters for the same header.
Rows are reservoirs: group by state + Gas Field Code to get storage fields (360 active fields in RP7 2024 and in RP8 August 2026).
Filter Status = 'Active' for operating fields; for the latest month in RP8 keep the maximum Month value of the latest year.
Join to PHMSA UNGS Part B on Gas Field Code to add facility coordinates.
reading_traps: Column letters are not stable between reports: Working Gas Capacity is 'm' in RP7 and 'n' in RP8.
Maximum Daily Delivery is a withdrawal rate; no injection-rate field is published.
Company Name is the EIA-191 respondent and can differ in spelling from the PHMSA operator name (e.g. 'ENSTOR KATY STORAGE & TRANSPLP' vs 'KATY STORAGE & TRANSPORTATION LP').
Inactive rows keep their capacities (23 of 28 inactive rows in RP7 2024 have working gas capacity above 0): filter Status = Active before summing.
Field counts depend on the key: RP7 2024 has 386 active reservoir rows but 360 active fields (state + Gas Field Code); EIA's capacity report counts 375 active Lower 48 fields as of November 2025.
RP7 annual for 2024 has 3 rows with empty Base Gas, 5 with empty or 0 working gas capacity and 9 with empty or 0 Maximum Daily Delivery.

problems: No published API documentation: endpoint taken from the NGQS web application script (app.min.js).

evidence.claim: The capacity report points to field-level data.

evidence.quote: A facility is “inactive” if it has not had any injections for at least the twelve months prior to this report month, and does not contain volumes of working gas, or is in the process of abandonment or depletion.

We calculate total design capacity as the sum of the reported working natural gas capacities of the 375 active storage fields in the Lower 48 states as reported on Form EIA-191, Monthly Underground Natural Gas Storage Report , as of November 2025.

how_to_use.example_result: DATAFILE_AS_OF=2/2/2026, REPORT_YEAR=2024, OPERATOR_ID=31705, OPERATOR_NAME=KATY STORAGE & TRANSPORTATION LP, PARTB_UNGS_FACILITY_NAME=Enstor Katy, PARTB_INTER_INTRA=Intra, PARTB_LOCATION_LATITUDE=29.75160, PARTB_LOCATION_LONGITUDE=-95.80377, TX, FORT BEND, PARTB_EIA_GAS_FIELD_CODE=370123, WORKING 23.5, BASE 7.8, TOTAL 31.3 BCF
steps: Download the ZIP from phmsa.dot.gov (rejects automated clients) or the same file attached to data.transportation.gov dataset aemm-7pyq (older build).
Open 'UNGS AR <year> Part B.csv' (latin-1 encoding); one row per facility.
Drop trailing empty rows (rows with empty OPERATOR_ID): 57 of 450 rows in the 2025 file.
Use Part C (same year) for reservoir type and in-service year; join on OPERATOR_ID + PARTB_UNGS_FACILITY_NAME.
Join to EIA RP7/RP8 on state + PARTB_EIA_GAS_FIELD_CODE (zero-padded to 6 digits) to add Active/Inactive status and maximum daily delivery; 303 of 396 facilities matched in 2024.
reading_traps: The CSV files end with blank rows (57 of 450 in 2025 Part B) that inflate row counts.
Withdrawn/injected volumes are annual metered volumes, not injection or withdrawal capacity.
No status field: a facility present in the latest year is reported, not necessarily active; use EIA status.
All 393 facility points of 2025 fall inside the bounding box of their declared state (checked), but they are operator-reported single points for fields that can cover several km2.
The data.transportation.gov attachment lags the phmsa.dot.gov ZIP (report year 2024 vs 2025 when tested).

PARTB_EIA_GAS_FIELD_CODE is operator-entered: 93 of 396 codes in 2024 do not exist in EIA RP7 (some look like county FIPS codes such as '129' or '147'), and 28 of 264 one-to-one matches differ by more than 5% in working gas capacity.

problems: www.phmsa.dot.gov returns 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai) to automated clients for the data page and the ZIP; tested file is the copy attached to data.transportation.gov (report year 2024, DATAFILE_AS_OF 2/2/2026).
The 2025 report-year figures in this record come from the Wayback Machine copy of the PHMSA ZIP dated 2026-05-08.

Several terminals report TYPE_OF_FACILITY 'Base Load' with function 'Storage w/ Liquefaction' (e.g. Freeport) instead of a marine-terminal function.

steps: Pick the newest quarterly file from the 'U.S. liquefaction capacity' dropdown on https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (file name pattern U.S.liquefactioncapacity_YYYY_Qn.xlsx).
Sheet 'Existing & Under Construction': headers in rows 2-3 (units in row 3), one row per train or train group; blank separator rows between projects; notes start at row 60.
Sheet 'Approved': headers in rows 3-4, projects in rows 5-13, footnotes below.
Strip footnote letters from capacity values (e.g. '0.80D', '6.20^') before converting to numbers.
reading_traps: Capacities carry footnote markers inside the cell ('0.66B', '13.33^'): they are text, not numbers.
Some rows aggregate several trains (e.g. 'Trains 1-18E'): the per-train columns then hold the group total (see notes E and F).
In-service date is the first commissioning cargo, not commercial operation; future dates are sponsor announcements ('2H2026').
Plaquemines LNG Phase 1 shows 'Commissioning' while PHMSA lists Plaquemines LNG as 'In Service' since 5/17/2024: different status definitions.

Status text is not normalised: 3Q 2026 has 'Under construction', 'Under Construction' and 'Under constructionH' (footnote letter appended); the 39 rows of the Existing sheet are 20 Commercial operation, 4 Commissioning and 15 under construction.

if_unstructured.summary: Proposed and planned LNG terminals and storage projects (and their county, capacity and docket) are found in FERC notices published in the Federal Register; the dockets lead to full filings in FERC eLibrary.
recipe: Query the Federal Register API for FERC notices (agency filter federal-energy-regulatory-commission) with terms such as "LNG terminal" or "storage field" "working gas" and a publication-date window; read each result's raw_text_url.

From each notice take the docket number from the '[Docket No. ...]' line: PF dockets are pre-filing (planned), CP dockets are filed applications (proposed); notices of availability of EA/EIS and later orders mark later stages.

Take the sponsor and county/parish from the first paragraph and capacity from 'Summary of the Proposed Project' (Mtpa for LNG export, Bcf working/cushion gas for storage); not every notice states capacity (the Longboard LNG import notice does not).

Deduplicate by docket: one project produces several notices (Rio Grande LNG Train 6 has a pre-filing scoping notice on 2026-03-12, a notice of application on 2026-06-12 and the CP26-532-000 notice of intent on 2026-08-03, which cites pre-filing docket PF26-3-000).
Check against the EIA liquefaction file (FERC docket column) to separate approved/under-construction export projects from proposals, and against PHMSA files once in service.
if_unstructured.location_method: Notices give county/parish and a site description (e.g. 'along the Brownsville Ship Channel in Cameron County, Texas'); location maps are appendices filed in FERC eLibrary under the docket, not in the Federal Register. Exact positions of existing LNG plants are held in NPMS (restricted).
cross_with: EIA U.S. Liquefaction Capacity file (FERC and DOE docket columns) for approval/FID/construction status of export projects.
DOE 'Summary of LNG Export Applications' (as of 2026-09-30) for DOE export authorization status per applicant.
PHMSA LNG and UNGS annual report files for facilities once in service.
FERC eLibrary (https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search) by docket number for applications, maps and orders.

where_published.name: Federal Register – FERC notices (LNG terminals)
where_published.what: FERC notices of pre-filing scoping, application, intent to prepare EIS/EA and schedules for LNG terminal projects, with docket numbers (PF = pre-filing, CP = application), county/parish and project summary.
where_published.how_to_search_inside: Public JSON API: /api/v1/documents.json with conditions[term]="LNG terminal", conditions[agencies][]=federal-energy-regulatory-commission and conditions[publication_date][gte]; 21 notices for 2026. Full text at the document's raw_text_url.

example_document.what_it_gives: Rio Grande LNG Expansion Project notice of intent (2026-08-03): '[Docket No. CP26-532-000]'; 'Rio Grande LNG Train 6, LLC (Rio Grande LNG) in Cameron County, Texas'; 'would produce about 6.03 million tonnes per annum of liquified natural gas (LNG) for export' (Summary of the Proposed Project).

where_published.name: Federal Register – FERC notices (underground storage projects)
where_published.what: FERC notices for new or expanded storage fields and caverns with county, working gas and cushion gas.
where_published.how_to_search_inside: Same API with conditions[term]="storage field" "working gas" and the FERC agency filter; 4 notices for 2026.

example_document.what_it_gives: Petal Cavern Expansion Project scoping notice (2026-05-05): '[Docket No. CP26-127-000]'; 'Gulf South Pipeline, LLC (Gulf South) in Forrest County, Mississippi'; 'a new salt dome storage cavern with a total capacity of 16 billion cubic feet (Bcf), including 10.0 Bcf of working gas and 6.0 Bcf of cushion gas' (Summary of the Proposed Project).

open_questions: Sabine Pass liquefaction capacity differs by publisher: PHMSA LIQUEFACTION_RATE 5100 MMCF/D (2024 and 2025), EIA six trains of 0.59 Bcf/d baseload and 0.76 Bcf/d peak, Cheniere 'more than 4.7 billion cubic feet per day' processed; definitions are not reconciled in the documents.
